questions.stem: What does 「休みの日は、家でごろごろしています。」 mean?
options: On my days off, I visit my family's home
On my days off, I laze around at home
On my days off, I clean up the house
On my days off, I study at home all day
questions.explanation: 「ごろごろする」 describes lounging about doing nothing in particular. It is a common, slightly self-mocking way to describe a relaxed day off. Cleaning would be 「そうじする」.

questions.stem: What is 「ゴールデンウィーク」 in Japan?
options: A week-long school holiday at the end of August
Public holidays from late April to early May
A week of department store sales in midsummer
The New Year holidays at the start of January
questions.explanation: Golden Week is a cluster of public holidays around the end of April and the start of May, one of the busiest travel periods of the year. The New Year break is 「お正月」.

questions.stem: What do people do when they go 「もみじがり」?
options: Go out to look at the autumn leaves
Pick fruit in orchards in autumn
Rake up fallen leaves in their garden
Go hunting in the mountains in autumn
questions.explanation: 「もみじ」 are maple leaves, and although 「がり」 comes from 'hunting', もみじがり means going out to admire the autumn colours. Like お花見 in spring, it is leisure built around the seasons.

questions.stem: 「日本では、春のお花見や秋のもみじがりのように、きせつを楽しむレジャーが多い。」 What does the sentence say about leisure in Japan?
options: Leisure activities change because the weather is poor
People prefer outdoor leisure in the colder seasons
Many leisure activities centre on enjoying the seasons
Most leisure activities take place in spring and autumn
questions.explanation: 「きせつを楽しむレジャー」 is leisure for enjoying the seasons, and 「〜のように」 gives cherry-blossom and autumn-leaf viewing as examples. It does not say most leisure happens only in those two seasons.

questions.stem: 「おんせんでは、ゆぶねに入る前に体をあらいます。」 Why is this the custom?
options: So the staff can see which guests have already paid
So the shared bath water stays clean for everyone
So the body gets used to cold water before the bath
So that guests spend less time in the changing room
questions.explanation: The 「ゆぶね」 is the bathtub that everyone shares, so you wash and rinse at the taps first and get into the bath clean. The bath is for soaking, not for washing.

questions.stem: What is 「ラジオたいそう」?
options: A sports commentary broadcast live on the radio
An exercise class run for staff at radio stations
Light exercises done along to a radio broadcast
A radio programme that reports sports news each morning
questions.explanation: ラジオたいそう is a short routine of exercises done along with piano music and spoken instructions, broadcast on radio since 1928. It shows how a shared daily routine can become part of a lifestyle.

questions.stem: 「日本の学校では、多くのせいとが、ほうかごだけでなく週まつにも部活のれんしゅうをします。」 What does this suggest about leisure for many Japanese students?
options: They have no interest in sport outside school
They practise only after school on weekdays
Their weekends are kept free for family outings
Club activities take up much of their free time
questions.explanation: 「〜だけでなく〜にも」 means 'not only... but also', so club practice happens after school and at weekends too. For many students the club is the centre of their leisure time.

questions.stem: 「コンビニでは、おべんとうをあたためてもらえるし、お金も下ろせるので、とてもべんりです。」 What does the writer say about convenience stores?
options: You can have a boxed meal heated and withdraw money
You can buy a boxed meal and send money overseas
You can heat your own lunch and pay bills at the counter
You can order a boxed meal and have money delivered
questions.explanation: 「あたためてもらえる」 is 'can have it heated for you' (もらう in the potential), and 「お金を下ろす」 is to withdraw cash. 「し」 links the two reasons the writer finds them convenient.

questions.stem: At a restaurant, a friend says 「今日はわりかんにしよう。」 What is the friend suggesting?
options: Let's take the leftovers home today
Let's split the bill evenly today
Let me pay for everyone today
Let's order one more dish today
questions.explanation: 「わりかん」 is splitting a bill equally, common among friends, and 「しよう」 is the volitional of 「する」, 'let's'. Treating everyone would be 「おごる」.

questions.stem: 「週まつは、家族で近くの山へハイキングに行くことにしています。」 What does 〜ことにしています express?
options: A rule that someone else set for the family
An outing the family is unable to make this year
A habit the family decided on and keeps to
A plan the family has just made for one weekend
questions.explanation: 「〜ことにする」 is to decide to do something, and 「〜ことにしている」 is the continuing result: a practice the speaker has chosen and keeps. A single new plan would be 「〜ことにしました」.

questions.stem: 「しんかんせんができて、東京からおおさかまで日帰りで行けるようになりました。」 What change does the sentence describe?
options: People started moving from Tokyo to Osaka
A night train between Tokyo and Osaka began
A Tokyo-Osaka day trip became possible
The trip from Tokyo to Osaka became cheaper
questions.explanation: 「行けるようになりました」 combines the potential 「行ける」 with 「ようになる」: it became possible to go. 「日帰り」 is a return trip in one day. The first shinkansen line opened in 1964.

questions.stem: 「インスタントラーメンは、一九五八年に日本で生まれました。おゆを入れるだけで食べられるので、生活がべんりになりました。」 Why did it make life more convenient?
options: It can be kept in the fridge for a long time
It is cheaper than cooking rice at home
You can eat it just by adding hot water
You can buy it at any restaurant in Japan
questions.explanation: 「おゆを入れるだけで食べられる」 means it can be eaten just by adding hot water. Ando Momofuku launched the first instant ramen in 1958 and the cup version in 1971.

questions.stem: 「一九七九年にソニーのウォークマンが出て、外を歩きながら音楽が聞けるようになりました。」 How did this change leisure?
options: People could hear music while out walking
People could record music in their own homes
People began walking to concerts in the city
People could listen to the radio in the car
questions.explanation: 「歩きながら」 is 'while walking', and 「聞けるようになりました」 is 'became able to listen'. A portable player turned music into something you could take anywhere.

questions.stem: The word 'emoji' comes from Japanese. What are its parts?
options: え (picture) and 文字 (character)
えがお (smile) and 文字 (character)
English 'emotion' and じ (letter)
English 'emoticon', shortened
questions.explanation: Emoji is 「え」 (picture) + 「文字」 (character): picture characters. The likeness to the English word 'emotion' is a coincidence. An early, widely used set was designed in Japan in 1999 for mobile phones.

questions.stem: 「えいがかんに行かなくても、家で新しいえいがが見られるようになりました。」 What does the sentence say?
options: People must now go to the cinema if they want to see new films
People stopped watching new films once they could stay at home
People can now see new films at the cinema without leaving early
People can now watch new films at home without going to the cinema
questions.explanation: 「行かなくても」 is 'even without going', and 「見られるようになりました」 is 'have become able to watch'. Streaming has moved some film-going into the home.

questions.stem: 「スマホのゲームの中には、外を歩かないとあそべないものもあって、運動するきっかけになっている。」 What effect does the writer describe?
options: Some games need you to walk outside, which gets people moving
Some phone games stop people walking outside, so they get less exercise
Phone games are only allowed outside, so children must play them in parks
Walking outside is more fun than phone games, so people play them less
questions.explanation: 「歩かないとあそべない」 is a double negative: if you don't walk, you can't play. 「きっかけになる」 is to become the trigger for something, here exercise. The effect described is positive.

questions.stem: 「子どもが家でゲームをする時間がふえて、外であそぶ時間がへったと言う親が多い。」 What concern does the sentence report?
options: Children play outside less as gaming at home grows
Children game outside more and spend less time at home
Parents spend more time gaming and less time outside
Children have less time for both games and outdoor play
questions.explanation: 「ふえる」 (increase) applies to gaming at home and 「へる」 (decrease) to playing outside. 「〜と言う親が多い」 reports what many parents say.

questions.stem: 「歩いたかずをかぞえるアプリを使うようになってから、前よりよく歩くようになりました。」 What does the speaker say?
options: Since I started walking more, I use a step-counting app
A step-counting app told me I walk less than before
I walk as much as before, even with a step-counting app
Since using a step-counting app, I walk more than before
questions.explanation: Both clauses use 「ようになる」, a change in habit: starting to use the app, and as a result walking more. 「〜てから」 fixes the order: the app came first.

questions.stem: What made おおたにしょうへい's career in Major League Baseball stand out?
options: He played for one team for over twenty years
He became a coach while still playing
He starred as both a pitcher and a hitter
He was the first Japanese player in the league
questions.explanation: Ohtani is known as a two-way player, starring both on the mound and at the plate, and was the unanimous American League MVP in 2021. He was not the first Japanese player in the major leagues.

questions.stem: Which achievement is はにゅうゆづる known for?
options: Olympic gold in men's gymnastics in 2016 and 2020
Olympic gold in men's figure skating in 2014 and 2018
Olympic gold in men's figure skating in 2010 and 2014
Olympic gold in men's speed skating in 2014 and 2018
questions.explanation: Hanyu won the men's figure skating title at Sochi in 2014 and PyeongChang in 2018, the first man to win it twice in a row since Dick Button in 1948 and 1952.

questions.stem: Which first does おおさかなおみ hold?
options: First player to win all four Grand Slams in one year
First Japanese player to win a Grand Slam singles title
First Japanese player to win a Grand Slam doubles title
First Asian player to win an Olympic tennis gold medal
questions.explanation: Osaka won the US Open in 2018, the first Grand Slam singles title by a Japanese player, and in 2019 became the first Asian player ranked number one in singles. Japanese players had won Grand Slam doubles titles decades earlier.

questions.stem: うただひかる's 1999 album 『First Love』 is known for what?
options: Being the best-selling album in Japan's history
Being the first Japanese album to top the US chart
Being sung entirely in English for overseas fans
Being the first album sold only online in Japan
questions.explanation: First Love is generally recognised as the best-selling album ever in Japan, with sales of well over seven million copies there. It was released on CD in 1999, long before online-only releases.

questions.stem: In こんどうまりえ's KonMari method of tidying, how do you decide whether to keep something?
options: Keep it only if it fits into one box
Keep it only if it sparks joy (ときめく)
Keep it only if you used it in the past year
Keep it only if it is worth some money
questions.explanation: Kondo asks people to tidy by category and keep only what sparks joy, 「ときめく」. Her 2019 Netflix series spread the idea worldwide, an example of a Japanese speaker shaping lifestyles abroad.

questions.stem: The artist くさまやよい is famous for art featuring what?
options: Ink-brush landscapes of misty mountains
Woodblock prints of kabuki actors
Clay figures of anime characters
Polka dots and mirrored infinity rooms
questions.explanation: Kusama's work is known for its dense polka dots (みずたま) and her infinity mirror rooms, including mirrored rooms filled with dotted pumpkins. Woodblock prints of actors belong to the Edo-period ukiyo-e artists.

questions.stem: 「おおたにせんしゅは、多くの子どもたちに夢をあたえました。」 What does 「夢をあたえる」 mean here?
options: To inspire people with hope
To give people presents they dreamed of
To send people off to sleep peacefully
To tell people about one's own dreams
questions.explanation: 「夢をあたえる」, literally 'give dreams', means to inspire people, especially the young, to aim high. It is a set phrase for describing a public figure's influence.

questions.stem: In a response about a sports star, which sentence evaluates the person's contribution rather than just giving a fact?
options: 「おおたにせんしゅは、日本の東北地方で生まれました。」
「おおたにせんしゅのおかげで、日本のやきゅうを見る人が世界中でふえたと思います。」
「おおたにせんしゅは、2021年にアメリカでMVPにえらばれました。」
「おおたにせんしゅは、ピッチャーとバッターの両方をします。」
questions.explanation: 「〜のおかげで」 credits the player with a result, and 「〜と思います」 marks it as the writer's judgement, so the sentence evaluates. The others report facts about awards, playing role and birthplace.

questions.stem: What is 「まんざい」?
options: Comic storytelling by one kneeling performer
A theatre of puppets with a chanter
A comic song sung by a large group
Comedy by a duo in quick-fire dialogue
questions.explanation: Manzai is stand-up comedy by a pair of performers trading lines at speed. Comic storytelling by one kneeling performer is らくご.

questions.stem: In a まんざい duo, what does the 「ボケ」 do?
options: Points out and corrects the partner's mistakes
Introduces the act and thanks the audience
Plays music between the parts of the act
Says or does something silly or mistaken
questions.explanation: The ボケ makes the silly remark or mistake, and the ツッコミ points it out, often with a sharp retort. The laugh comes from the exchange between the two roles.

questions.stem: A: 「明日は日曜日だから、学校に行こう！」 B: 「いや、日曜日は学校は休みだよ！」 Which まんざい role is B playing?
options: ボケ
しかい
きゃく
ツッコミ
questions.explanation: B corrects A's absurd suggestion (going to school on a Sunday), which is the ツッコミ's job. A, who says the silly thing, is the ボケ.

questions.stem: What is the M-1 Grand Prix?
options: An annual car race held in Japan since 2001
An annual prize for new manga, first awarded in 2001
An annual competition for まんざい duos, first held in 2001
An annual music chart for Japanese pop songs, begun in 2001
questions.explanation: The M-1 Grand Prix is a yearly televised contest for manzai acts that began in 2001. Its finals are watched as a major event in Japanese comedy.

questions.stem: A student tastes a dessert and says happily 「このケーキ、やばい！」 What does she mean?
options: This cake is amazing!
This cake has gone off!
This cake is too sweet!
This cake is too dear!
questions.explanation: 「やばい」 first meant risky or bad, but young speakers also use it for a strong positive reaction. Her happy tone shows she means 'amazing'. The same word can mean 'awful' in another context.

questions.stem: What is 「おしかつ」?
options: Spending time and money supporting a favourite performer
Practising hard to win a place in a school club
Studying hard to pass university entrance exams
Working part-time to save up for an overseas trip
questions.explanation: An 「おし」 is the performer or character you support most, and おしかつ is everything fans do for them: buying goods, going to concerts, sharing their work. It shows how fandom shapes young people's leisure.

questions.stem: What is はつねミク?
options: The heroine of a long-running anime about a high school band
A robot built by a university to sing at concerts in Japan
A character whose singing voice is software, singing fans' songs
An idol singer who began on a TV talent show and later went solo
questions.explanation: Hatsune Miku is the character of a singing voice synthesiser: users type in melody and lyrics and the software sings them. Many of her songs are written by fans, and she 'performs' at concerts as a projection.

questions.stem: 「日本のドラマは、ふつう一つのきせつに十話ぐらいで終わる。」 What does the sentence say?
options: A Japanese drama usually begins ten episodes before each season
A Japanese drama usually ends after about ten episodes
A Japanese drama usually runs for about ten seasons
A Japanese drama usually shows about ten episodes each week
questions.explanation: 「話」 is the counter for episodes, and 「一つのきせつに」 is 'within one season'. Many Japanese dramas tell a complete story in about three months.

questions.stem: 「人気ドラマに出てきたカフェに、ファンがたくさん行くようになった。」 What happened?
options: A café began showing a popular drama to its customers
Fans began visiting a café that appeared in a popular drama
A popular drama was filmed in a café that fans run
Fans of a café started making a popular drama about it
questions.explanation: 「出てきた」 is 'appeared (in the drama)', and 「行くようになった」 is a change: fans started going. It shows how youth entertainment influences what people do.

questions.stem: 「『かわいい』ということばは、今では英語でも使われるほど、世界に知られている。」 What does 〜ほど show?
options: A limit: known only as far as English is spoken
A reason: known because it is used in English
The degree: so well known it is even used in English
A comparison: better known than English words
questions.explanation: 「〜ほど」 sets the extent: the word is known worldwide to the point of being used in English. That reveals how far Japanese youth culture has travelled.

questions.stem: 「まんがやアニメ、J-POPは、日本の若者だけでなく世界中の若者にえいきょうをあたえている。」 What claim is made?
options: They influence young people in Japan more than elsewhere
They are influenced by young people around the world
They influence only young people who live in Japan
They influence young people worldwide, not only in Japan
questions.explanation: 「えいきょうをあたえる」 is to have an influence on, and 「〜だけでなく」 widens it from Japan's young people to young people around the world. The influence flows outward from Japan.
